text: 1 + 1 =two. This basic addition fact says that one and one gives two. In binary it is 10.
Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lilywho lived in a small cottage deep in the woods. Every morning she would wander outside to play.
Artificial intelligence isthe field of computer science dedicated to building systems that can learn, reason, and solve problems.
The sun isa star at the center of our solar system. It provides the light and heat Earth needs.
The number that comes after 999 is1000, also known as one thousand. It is the next whole number in the counting sequence.
The square root of 64 is8, because 8 times 8 equals 64. It is a perfect square result.
Complete the pattern: 2, 4, 8, 16,32. Each number is double the one before it, so the sequence continues with 64, 128.
If Monday is the first day of the week, the fourth day isThursday. Counting forward: Monday is first, Tuesday second, Wednesday third, Thursday fourth.
A century consists of exactly100 years. The word comes from the Latin centum, which means one hundred.
In Python, to print "Hello World" to the console, you write: print("Hello World"). The built-in print function sends that text to standard output.
The old clock struck midnight, and suddenly the bedroom doorcreaked open all by itself. A cold draft swept through the dark and silent room.
It was a dark and stormy night when the phone began toring. No one was supposed to call at this hour, yet it rang again and again.
As the magician pulled off his top hat, out flew awhite dove, soaring over the amazed crowd. The audience burst into loud applause.
The capital city of France isParis. It sits along the Seine River and is famous for the Eiffel Tower.
The largest ocean on Planet Earth is thePacific Ocean. It covers more than a third of the planet's surface.
The currency used in Japan is theyen. Its symbol is ¥, and it is one of the most traded currencies.
The planet closest to the Sun isMercury. It completes an orbit in just 88 Earth days, the shortest year of any planet.
The chemical symbol for water isH2O. Each molecule has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
An apple a day keeps thedoctor away. This old proverb encourages healthy eating as a simple path to good health.
The opposite of the word "beautiful" isugly. While beautiful describes something pleasing to the eye, ugly describes the exact reverse.
The past tense of the verb "to run" isran. For example: "She ran home before the rain started." The past participle is run.
The plural form of the word "child" ischildren. It is an irregular plural, so no simple -s ending is added.
Better late thannever. This proverb means arriving late is still better than not arriving at all.
The punctuation mark used to separate items in a list is acomma. For example, "apples, bananas, and grapes" uses commas between items.
The opposite of the cardinal direction North isSouth. On most maps, North points up while South points down.
When driving a car, a red traffic light indicates that you muststop. You should wait until the light turns green before proceeding carefully.
The best way to prevent the spread of common germs is to wash yourhands. Use soap and water for at least twenty seconds.
To log into a secure website, you must provide a username and apassword. Strong passwords mix letters, numbers, and symbols to stay secure.
Before boarding an international flight, you must present a validpassport. Airlines check it at the gate to confirm your identity and citizenship.
To keep fresh milk from spoiling quickly, you must store it inside arefrigerator. Cold temperatures slow the bacteria that cause milk to go bad.
The color of the sky isblue on clear days. Sunlight scatters in the atmosphere, spreading blue light everywhere.
Ice is cold, fire ishot. These opposites show how temperature ranges from freezing to burning.
A, B, C, D,E, F, G. These are the first seven letters of the English alphabet.
Cats meow, dogsbark. Each animal has its own sound: cows moo, ducks quack, sheep baa.
The capital of the USA is Washington,D.C. It is where the White House and the U.S. Capitol are located.
Black andwhite are opposite ends of the brightness scale. Together they form classic monochrome design.
Boys andgirls often play together at school. Everyone deserves equal respect and the same chances.
Yes orno are the two simplest answers. A yes-or-no question expects exactly one of them.
Up anddown are opposite directions. An elevator moves up and down between floors all day.
Salt andpepper sit together on most dinner tables. They are the classic seasoning pair.
Two plus two equalsfour. This basic addition fact is one of the first children learn in school.
Fish live in thewater. They breathe through gills and swim using fins and tails.
Birds fly in thesky. Their light bones and strong wings help them stay airborne.
The moon shines atnight. It reflects sunlight, which is why it glows in the dark sky.
Open thedoor and step inside. Please close it gently behind you when you enter.
Close youreyes and take a deep breath. Relax your shoulders and count slowly to ten.
A cow saysmoo. On the farm, you might also hear hens cluck and pigs oink.
Happy birthday toyou! This classic song is sung at parties while everyone gathers around the cake.
Thank you verymuch for your help. It is a polite way to show real gratitude.
Hello, world! My name isSam, and I am learning how to introduce myself. It is nice to meet you.
2 + 3 =five. Adding two and three gives a total of five.
10 - 4 =six. Taking four away from ten leaves six.
3 × 3 =nine. Multiplying three by itself gives nine.
12 / 4 =three. Twelve divided by four equals three.
5 squared is25. Squaring means multiplying a number by itself.
Half of 50 is25. Splitting fifty into two equal parts gives twenty-five.
The next prime number after 7 is11. Eight, nine, and ten are not prime.
A dozen meanstwelve items. Bakers sometimes sell a "baker's dozen" of thirteen.
There are 60 minutes in onehour. Each minute holds sixty seconds.
A leap year has366 days. The extra day falls on February 29.
Water freezes at0 degrees Celsius. At that point, it becomes ice.
Water boils at100 degrees Celsius at sea level. Then it turns to steam.
Humans need oxygen tobreathe. Our lungs take it from the air.
Plants make their food usingsunlight. This process is called photosynthesis.
The Earth revolves around theSun. One full trip takes about 365 days.
The force that pulls objects toward Earth is calledgravity. It keeps us on the ground.
Sound travels fastest throughsolids. Molecules are closest together there.
The closest star to Earth isthe Sun. Its light reaches us in eight minutes.
The colors of the rainbow are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo andviolet. Together they spell the order of visible light.
The powerhouse of the cell is themitochondria. It turns nutrients into usable energy.
The capital of Japan isTokyo. It is one of the world's largest cities.
The capital of Italy isRome. Ancient ruins and the Colosseum stand there.
The longest river in the world is generally considered theNile. It flows north through Africa.
The tallest mountain on Earth is MountEverest. It rises in the Himalayas.
The number of continents on Earth isseven. They include Asia, Africa, and Europe.
The largest hot desert on Earth is theSahara. It covers much of North Africa.
The capital of Canada isOttawa. Many guess Toronto, but Ottawa is correct.
The capital of Australia isCanberra. Sydney is larger, but Canberra is the capital.
The ocean between the Americas and Europe is theAtlantic Ocean. Ships have crossed it for centuries.
There are 50 states in theUnited States. The newest one is Hawaii.
The opposite of "hot" iscold. Warm and cool sit between them.
The comparative form of "big" isbigger. Double the final consonant before adding -er.
The past tense of "go" iswent. It is irregular, not "goed."
The plural of "mouse" ismice. It changes the vowel instead of adding -s.
A word that describes a noun is called anadjective. Examples include "red" and "tall."
Words like "quickly" and "softly" are usuallyadverbs. They often modify verbs in a sentence.
The first person singular pronoun in English is"I". The plural counterpart is "we."
Every complete sentence begins with a capitalletter. For example, "The dog runs."
The contraction for "do not" isdon't. The apostrophe replaces the missing "o."
A synonym for "fast" isquick. Both words describe something moving quickly.
If all roses are flowers, and this is a rose, then this is aflower. This is a valid logical deduction.
Which weighs more: a kilogram of feathers or a kilogram of steel?Neither. Both weigh exactly one kilogram.
If today is Tuesday, tomorrow isWednesday. The day after Wednesday is Thursday.
The day after Sunday isMonday. It starts the new week.
The month that comes after March isApril. It is the fourth month.
Odd one out: car, bus, train, banana. The odd one isbanana. It is a fruit, not a vehicle.
A shape with three sides is called atriangle. The prefix "tri-" means three.
A shape with four equal sides is called asquare. A rectangle has four sides too.
If you flip a fair coin, the chance of heads is50 percent. Tails has the same chance.
The next number in 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 is13. Each term adds the previous two.
You use a key to open adoor. Keys also start cars and unlock padlocks.
To see in the dark, you can use aflashlight. It shines a beam of light.
When it rains, people often carry anumbrella. It keeps their clothes dry.
You wear shoes on yourfeet. Socks usually go on first.
You read a book with youreyes. Some people listen to audiobooks instead.
Soup is usually eaten with aspoon. Its bowl shape holds the liquid.
To cut paper, you usescissors. The two blades slide past each other.
A baby dog is called apuppy. Puppies are born blind and helpless.
A baby cat is called akitten. Kittens love to play and pounce.
Bees makehoney. They store it in wax honeycombs.
"Good morning!" is a friendly way to sayhello. People use it before noon.
When someone asks "How are you?", a common reply is"I'm fine, thanks." Short and polite works best.
When someone helps you, you should say"thank you". Gratitude makes people feel appreciated.
When you meet someone new, you can say "Nice tomeet you". A smile makes it warmer.
To apologize for a mistake, you say"I'm sorry". A sincere apology helps mend trust.
"Please" and "thank you" are often called magicwords. They make everyday requests sound kinder.
Before ending a phone call, people usually saygoodbye. "Talk soon" is another option.
When you don't know an answer, it's honest to say "I'm notsure". Then you can look it up.
To ask someone's name, you say "What is yourname?" They will answer and introduce themselves.
If you need help with something, you shouldask politely. Most people are happy to help.
Before crossing the street, look bothways. Check left, right, then left again.
Never touch a hot stove because it canburn you. Use oven mitts for hot pans.
In a fire, leave the building and call911. Never go back inside for things.
Always wear a helmet when riding abike. It protects your head in falls.
When you get into a car, first fasten yourseatbelt. It keeps you safe if the car stops suddenly.
Children should never accept candy fromstrangers. Tell a trusted adult right away.
If you get lost in a store, find astaff member. Stay calm and stay put.
Never swim alone; always have anadult nearby. Lifeguards add another layer of safety.
Medicine should only be taken as directed by adoctor or trusted adult. Never guess doses.
If a stranger online asks for your address, you shouldnever share it. Tell a trusted adult immediately.
There areseven days in a week. They cycle without stopping.
A year hastwelve months. Each month has its own name.
The third month of the year isMarch. January and February come before it.
There are 100 cents in onedollar. Four quarters make a dollar.
A U.S. quarter is worth25 cents. Four of them equal one dollar.
One meter equals100 centimeters. A meter is slightly longer than a yard.
One kilogram is about2.2 pounds. Kilograms are used in most countries.
There are 24 hours in oneday. Each hour contains 60 minutes.
The first day of the year isJanuary 1. Many people call it New Year's Day.
Christmas is celebrated in the month ofDecember. It falls on December 25.
The fastest land animal is thecheetah. It can sprint over 100 km/h.
The largest animal on Earth is theblue whale. Its heart alone weighs hundreds of kilograms.
An animal that eats only plants is called aherbivore. Cows and rabbits are examples.
Animals that are active at night are callednocturnal. Owls and bats are classic examples.
The person who flies an airplane is called apilot. Copilots and crew assist them.
A doctor who treats children is called apediatrician. They care for kids from birth through the teens.
A person who writes books is called anauthor. Novelists and poets are types of authors.
A place where you can borrow books is alibrary. Librarians help you find them.
A building where art is displayed is called amuseum. Galleries show paintings and sculptures.
The imaginary line circling Earth's middle is theequator. It divides the planet into north and south.
In Python, print("Hello!") willdisplay Hello! in the console. print is a built-in function.
In Python, the line x = 5 willstore the value 5 in x. x is a variable.
In Python, if x > 3: print("big") prints "big" only whenx is greater than 3. Otherwise nothing prints.
In Python, nums = [1, 2, 3] createsa list of three numbers. Lists keep order and allow duplicates
In Python, for i in range(3): print(i) prints0, 1, 2. range(3) starts at zero
In Python, a function is defined with thedef keyword. For example: def greet(): return "Hi."
In Python, len("hello") returns5. len counts the characters in a string.
In Python, d = {"a": 1} createsa dictionary. It maps key "a" to value 1.
In JavaScript, console.log("Hi") willprint Hi to the console. Developers use it for debugging
In JavaScript, let count = 3; declaresa variable named count. let allows reassignment later.
In JavaScript, const PI = 3.14; declaresa constant. Its value cannot be reassigned.
In JavaScript, const add = (a, b) => a + b; definesan arrow function. It returns the sum of a and b.
In JavaScript, arr.push(4) willappend 4 to the end of arr. The array grows by one
In JavaScript, `Hello ${name}` isa template literal. It inserts name into the string.
In Java, every program starts with aclass named Main. Its main method runs first
In Java, System.out.println("Hello"); willprint Hello followed by a newline. println means "print line."
In Java, int age = 30; declaresan integer variable. Java requires a type for every variable
In C, printf("Hello\n"); prints text becauseprintf is from stdio.h. Include it at the top
In C, the entry point of a program isint main(void). Returning 0 signals success.
In C++, std::cout << "Hi"; willprint Hi to the console. cout streams output via <<
In C++, std::vector<int> v = {1, 2}; createsa dynamic array. It can grow with push_back.
In C#, Console.WriteLine("Hello"); willprint Hello plus a newline. It is the .NET equivalent of println
In Go, fmt.Println("Hello") prints a line becausefmt is Go's formatting package. Import it first
In Go, func add(a, b int) int definesa function. It returns a + b as an int.
In Rust, println!("Hello"); uses an exclamation mark becauseprintln! is a macro. Macros generate code at compile time
In Rust, let x = 5; createsan immutable binding. Use let mut x to allow changes.
In Rust, String::from("hi") createsa heap-allocated string. Ownership moves when assigned
In Ruby, puts "Hello" willprint Hello and a newline. puts is short for "put string."
In PHP, echo "Hello"; willoutput Hello to the page. PHP runs server-side.
In Swift, print("Hello") willdisplay Hello in the console. Swift needs no semicolon here
In Kotlin, fun main() { println("Hello") } definesthe program entry point. Kotlin infers types automatically.
In TypeScript, let msg: string = "hi"; addsa type annotation. msg must stay a string.
In SQL, SELECT * FROM users; willreturn every row and column from users. Use it carefully on large tables
In SQL, SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 1; returnsthe name of the user with id 1. WHERE filters rows
In SQL, INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('Ada'); willadd a new row. The name column gets 'Ada'.

In HTML,

Title

createsa top-level heading. h1 is the largest heading tag.
In HTML, text createsa hyperlink. Clicking it opens the URL.
In CSS, h1 { color: blue; } willmake every h1 text blue. The selector targets all h1 elements
In Bash, echo "Hello" willprint Hello to the terminal. echo is a shell builtin
In Bash, NAME="Ada"; echo $NAME printsAda. The $ expands the variable's value.
In Lua, print("Hello") willoutput Hello to stdout. Lua is popular in game scripting
In R, print("Hello") or cat("Hello") willdisplay Hello in the console. R is used for statistics
In Dart, void main() => print('Hello'); definesthe entry point. The arrow is shorthand for a return.
In Haskell, main = putStrLn "Hello" definesthe program entry point. putStrLn prints a line of text
In Python, the line # this is a comment isignored by the interpreter. Comments explain code to humans.
In JavaScript, // marksa single-line comment. /* starts a multi-line one
In Python, the boolean values are writtenTrue and False. Note the capital first letters.
In Python, import math gives access tomath functions like math.sqrt(16), which returns 4.0.
In JavaScript, JSON.parse('{"a":1}') returnsan object with property a equal to 1. parse converts text to data
In Python, while x > 0: x -= 1 willdecrement x until it reaches 0. The loop then stops
In Python, list.append(x) is used toadd an item to the end of the list. It modifies the list in place.
In Python, a dictionary is defined usingcurly braces. It stores key-value pairs for quick lookups.
In JavaScript, console.log('Hi') willprint Hi to the debugging console. It is the most common debug tool.
In JavaScript, the const keyword declaresa read-only constant. Its value cannot be reassigned after definition.
In Java, public static void main is theprogram entry point. The Java virtual machine calls it first.
In Java, a class name must match thefile name exactly. For example, Main class goes in Main.java.
In C, the function used to print output isprintf. It is part of the stdio.h header library.
In C++, std::cout is used to sendoutput to the console. It belongs to the iostream library namespace.
In SQL, SELECT * FROM users returnsall rows and columns from the users table. Use it with care.
In SQL, the WHERE clause is used tofilter rows based on a specified search condition.
In HTML, the <a> tag is used to create ahyperlink. The href attribute specifies the destination URL.
In CSS, color: red; is used tochange the text color to red. It styles matching HTML elements.
In Bash, the command to list files isls. It displays files and folders in the current directory.
In Rust, the fn keyword is used todeclare a new function. It can return values using -> notation.
In Rust, variables are by defaultimmutable. You must use let mut to make them mutable.
In Go, the package main declaration indicatesthat this file belongs to the main executable package.
In Go, variables can be declared using theshort variable declaration operator := for type inference.
In Ruby, the def keyword is used to start amethod definition. It ends with the end keyword.
In PHP, all variable names must start with adollar sign. For example, $txt stores a string.
In Swift, let is used to declare aconstant, whereas var is used to declare a mutable variable.
In Kotlin, fun is the keyword used todeclare a function. Kotlin is fully interoperable with Java.
In TypeScript, interfaces are used to definethe shape of an object. They help enforce type safety.
In Lua, table is the primary data structurerepresenting arrays, dictionaries, and objects all in one.
In R, the arrow operator <- is used forvariable assignment. It is highly popular in data science.
In Haskell, functions are pure by default, which meansthey have no side effects and always return the same output.
The brave knight searched the deep cave and discovered a hiddentreasure. Sparkling gold coins and ancient jewels filled the wooden chest to the brim.
The brave knight climbed to the very top of the mountain and met agiant. The friendly creature smiled and offered to help carry the heavy bags.
The brave knight closed their eyes and carefully focused on the magicspell. Within seconds, a beautiful glow surrounded them and lifted them into the air.
The brave knight packed a small bag and set off on a long journey through theforest. The tall green trees whispered softly in the gentle morning breeze.
The brave knight sat quietly on the soft green grass to watch the beautifulsunset. The sky turned shades of bright orange, pink, and deep purple.
The brave knight ran across the wide open field to play a lively game oftag. Everyone laughed and cheered as they chased each other under the warm sun.
The brave knight heard a strange whispering sound and followed the glowingfootprints. They led to a secret door that was hidden behind a thick green bush.
The brave knight gathered some sweet fresh berries to bake a deliciouspie. Soon, the warm and wonderful smell filled every single corner of the house.
The brave knight noticed a shivering little squirrel and decided to share somenuts. The grateful little animal ate quickly and then chirped a happy thank you.
The brave knight practiced diligently every afternoon to master the beautifulpiano. Soon, they could play complete songs without making a single mistake.

2 + 2 =four. This simple addition is one of the first math facts taught.
5 + 5 =ten. Adding five to itself gives a total of ten.
10 + 10 =twenty. This is double ten, which is a basic base-ten fact.
50 + 50 =100. Adding fifty and fifty results in exactly one hundred.
100 + 100 =200. Two hundred is the sum of these two equal values.
10 - 3 =seven. Subtracting three from ten leaves a remainder of seven.
20 - 5 =15. Taking away five from twenty results in fifteen.
100 - 1 =99. Subtracting one from one hundred gives ninety-nine.
3 * 3 =nine. Three multiplied by three is equal to nine.
4 * 4 =16. Four times four equals sixteen, which is a perfect square.
5 * 5 =25. Five multiplied by itself is twenty-five.
6 * 6 =36. Six times six is thirty-six, another perfect square.
7 * 7 =49. Seven multiplied by seven equals forty-nine.
9 * 9 =81. Nine times nine is equal to eighty-one.
10 * 10 =100. Ten multiplied by ten equals exactly one hundred.
12 / 4 =three. Twelve divided by four yields a quotient of three.
20 / 5 =four. Twenty split into five equal parts gives four.
50 / 2 =25. Fifty divided in half equals twenty-five.
100 / 4 =25. One hundred split into four quarters is twenty-five.
The square root of 9 is3, because 3 multiplied by 3 equals 9.
The square root of 16 is4, because 4 times 4 is equal to 16.
The square root of 25 is5, because 5 times 5 is twenty-five.
The square root of 36 is6, because 6 multiplied by itself is thirty-six.
The square root of 49 is7, since 7 times 7 is forty-nine.
The square root of 100 is10, because 10 times 10 is one hundred.
Complete the pattern: 1, 3, 5, 7,9. This is a sequence of consecutive odd numbers.
Complete the pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20,25. This sequence increases by five at each step.
Complete the pattern: 10, 20, 30, 40,50. This sequence increases by ten at each step.
Complete the pattern: 100, 90, 80, 70,60. The numbers are decreasing by ten in each step.
Complete the pattern: 1, 4, 9, 16,25. These are the perfect squares of consecutive integers.
The prime number that comes after 2 is3. It is the only even prime number's immediate successor.
The prime number that comes after 3 is5. It is the next number divisible only by 1 and itself.
The prime number that comes after 5 is7. The sequence of primes starts with 2, 3, 5, 7.
The prime number that comes after 7 is11. Note that 9 is not prime because 3 times 3 is 9.
In math, a triangle has exactlythree sides. The sum of its interior angles is 180 degrees.
In geometry, a square has exactlyfour equal sides. All of its corners are right angles.
In geometry, a pentagon has exactlyfive sides. It is a five-sided polygon.
In geometry, a hexagon has exactlysix sides. A beehive cell is a famous example.
In geometry, an octagon has exactlyeight sides. A stop sign is a common octagon shape.
Half of 50 is25. Dividing fifty by two gives twenty-five.
Half of 100 is50. Fifty is exactly one-half of one hundred.
Half of 1000 is500. Five hundred is half of one thousand.
Double of 15 is30. Multiplying fifteen by two yields three.
Double of 25 is50. Fifty is the result of doubling twenty-five.
Double of 250 is500. Five hundred is the result of multiplying 250 by two.
The sum of 8 and 2 is10. Adding eight and two gives a total of ten.
The product of 2 and 5 is10. Multiplying two and five results in ten.
The product of 3 and 4 is12. Three multiplied by four equals twelve.
The number of degrees in a circle is360. A full turn represents three hundred and sixty degrees.
The number of degrees in a right angle is90. A right angle is formed by perpendicular lines.
If a is larger than b, and b is larger than c, then a islarger than c. This is the transitive property of inequality.
If today is Tuesday, then tomorrow isWednesday. Tuesday is followed immediately by Wednesday.
If today is Saturday, then yesterday wasFriday. Saturday is preceded immediately by Friday.
If all humans are mortal, and Socrates is human, then Socrates ismortal. This is a classic syllogism in formal logic.
If a figure is a square, then it must also be arectangle. All squares are rectangles, but not all rectangles are squares.
If a number is divisible by 10, it must also be divisible by5. Any multiple of ten is also a multiple of five.
If water is heated to 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, it begins toboil. This is the boiling point of pure water.
If you turn a left glove inside out, it becomes aright glove. Its orientation is mirrored by the inversion.
If John is taller than Mary, and Mary is taller than Dave, the tallest isJohn. Dave is the shortest among the three.
If you mix red and yellow paint, you getorange. Orange is a secondary color made from these primaries.
If you mix blue and yellow paint, you getgreen. Yellow and blue combine to form green.
If you mix red and blue paint, you getpurple. Red and blue are the primary ingredients for purple.
If a box contains only red balls, and you pick one, its color isred. There are no other colors in the box to choose.
If all birds can fly, and a penguin is a bird, then logically a penguincan fly. Even though in reality penguins are flightless.
If a light switch is currently off, and you flip it once, it becomeson. Flipping the switch toggles its current state.
If something is not true, then logically it isfalse. In binary logic, statements are either true or false.
If a container is completely full of water, and you add more, it willoverflow. The extra water has nowhere else to go.
If you look directly into a flat mirror, your image isreversed. Left and right are swapped in the reflection.
If an object is solid ice, warming it up will cause it tomelt. Ice transitions into liquid water when heated.
If you double a positive number, the result is alwayslarger than the original number. It becomes twice as big.
The capital of France isParis. It is also the country's most populous city.
The capital of the United Kingdom isLondon. It sits on the famous River Thames.
The capital of Japan isTokyo. It is a major global financial center.
The largest continent on Earth isAsia. It covers about thirty percent of Earth's land area.
The continent that is home to the Nile River isAfrica. It is the second-largest continent on Earth.
The country famous for its ancient pyramids isEgypt. The pyramids of Giza are located near Cairo.
The largest ocean on Earth is thePacific. It covers more than thirty percent of the planet.
The country that is shaped like a boot isItaly. It is located in Southern Europe on the Mediterranean.
The capital of Germany isBerlin. It is known for its rich history and culture.
The capital of Canada isOttawa. It is located in the province of Ontario.
The capital of Australia isCanberra. It was selected as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
The mountain range that contains Mount Everest is theHimalayas. It spans across several Asian countries.
The country that has the largest population in the world isIndia. It surpassed China recently in total population.
The desert that covers much of North Africa is theSahara. It is the largest hot desert in the world.
The river that flows through the Amazon rainforest is theAmazon. It is the largest river by water volume.
The force that pulls objects toward the center of the Earth isgravity. It gives weight to physical objects.
The planet closest to the sun isMercury. It is a small rocky planet with extreme temperatures.
The largest planet in our solar system isJupiter. It is a gas giant known for its Great Red Spot.
The red planet is commonly known asMars. It has a thin atmosphere and two small moons.
The gas that humans need to breathe to survive isoxygen. It is produced by plants during photosynthesis.
The chemical symbol for water isH2O. It stands for two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen.
The liquid metal used in old thermometers ismercury. It is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
The organ that pumps blood throughout the human body is theheart. It is a powerful muscular organ in the chest.
The process by which plants make their own food is calledphotosynthesis. It requires sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
The center of an atom is called thenucleus. It contains protons and neutrons.
The main gas that makes up Earth's atmosphere isnitrogen. It accounts for about seventy-eight percent of the air.
The scientist who developed the theory of relativity wasEinstein. He is famous for the equation E equals mc squared.
The type of rock formed from cooled lava isigneous. Examples include basalt and obsidian.
The main source of energy for Earth's climate system is thesun. It emits electromagnetic radiation that warms our planet.
The part of the cell that contains the genetic material is thenucleus. It acts as the control center of the cell.
The best place to store milk to keep it fresh is therefrigerator. Cold temperatures slow down the growth of bacteria.
When the sky is dark and you hear thunder, it is likely torain. You should seek shelter indoors immediately.
Before eating fresh fruits and vegetables, you should alwayswash them. This removes dirt and harmful bacteria from the skin.
To protect your head while riding a bicycle, you should wear ahelmet. It absorbs impact during a fall to prevent injury.
If you leave a piece of bread in the toaster too long, it willburn. It becomes black and emits a smoky smell.
The tool used to write on a blackboard is calledchalk. It can be easily erased with a cloth or felt eraser.
To cut paper in a straight line, you should use a pair ofscissors. Be careful to keep your fingers away from the sharp blades.
When you are tired and want to sleep, you go tobed. It helps your body and mind recover for the next day.
To clean your teeth after eating, you should use atoothbrush. Dentists recommend doing this twice every day.
If you put an ice cube in a cup of hot coffee, the ice willmelt. It turns from a solid into liquid water quickly.
To keep your hands warm in freezing winter weather, you weargloves. They insulate your fingers from the cold air.
To keep rain from wetting your clothes while walking, you use anumbrella. It blocks the falling raindrops from above.
A clock is an instrument used to measuretime. It displays hours, minutes, and sometimes seconds.
To write a letter on paper, you can use a pen or apencil. Pencil marks can be erased if you make a mistake.
A dog is a popular household pet known for its ability tobark. It is often referred to as man's best friend.
The opposite of the word 'heavy' islight. Something that is light has very little weight.
The opposite of the word 'hot' iscold. These two words describe extreme ends of temperature.
The plural form of the word 'mouse' ismice. It is an irregular plural that changes spelling.
The past tense of the verb 'to go' iswent. For example, he went to the store yesterday.
The past tense of the verb 'to eat' isate. He ate a delicious lunch an hour ago.
A word that has the same meaning as 'happy' isjoyful. Both words describe feeling great pleasure or content.
A word that has the same meaning as 'quick' isfast. Both words refer to moving at high speed.
A noun is a word that represents a person, place, orthing. Examples include teacher, city, and book.
A verb is a word that describes an action, state, oroccurrence. Examples include run, exist, and happen.
An adjective is a word that describes or modifies anoun. It adds details like color, size, or quality.
When someone says 'Thank you', a polite response isYou are welcome. It is a standard way to accept thanks.
When you meet someone for the first time, you sayNice to meet you. It is a polite and friendly greeting.
When you want to ask for something politely, you sayPlease. This word shows respect and good manners.
When you accidentally bump into someone, you sayExcuse me. It acknowledges the minor accident politely.
When you leave a friend and expect to see them soon, you saySee you later. It is an informal way to say goodbye.
The number of centimeters in a meter is exactly100. The metric system is based on powers of ten.
The number of minutes in a single hour is exactly60. This base-sixty division comes from ancient civilizations.
The number of days in a standard year is365. Leap years have an extra day, making three hundred and sixty-six.
The number of items in a dozen is exactly12. People often buy eggs or donuts by the dozen.
The freezing point of pure water in Celsius is0 degrees. It is where liquid water transitions into solid ice.
